digest.component_or_area: comment hygiene detector and CI gate
propositions: Source code comments carry unresolvable commit SHAs, run IDs, and dated incident narratives that rot; 8+ cited SHAs in the tree are already unreachable due to Gerrit rebase-on-submit and retention window expiry.

A net-new block-level detector must scan comments and docstrings for rot-prone tokens (SHA-like hex >=7 chars, run/job/thread IDs >=8 digits, date+past-tense incident verb patterns) and reject them unless they cite a ticket system ID or use an external-context escape hatch.

All detector-hit sites in the tree must be remediated by either deleting rot-prone tokens, citing a resolvable ticket/epic/bug/story ID, or replacing SHA narratives with behavioral descriptions findable via git log.

The detector must avoid false positives on 'bug surfaced' (describes current state, not dated incident) and word-triple aliases in file paths, while accepting 4x4 hex-grouped IDs and sentence-final word-triple aliases as valid ticket references.

CI integration via scripts/check_comment_hygiene.py as a named step in _build-and-test.yml must block on reintroduced rot-prone refs and pass the remediated tree with zero in-tree suppressions and one structural self-exclusion.
Policy documentation in CONTRIBUTING.md must establish that source code comments own current state and concise rationale while the ticket system owns historical detail and dated incidents.
